items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I wrote some things with him... I used to play with him in Chicago.

ctx.x: Right. That means it was his best song.

Yeah, he could really play this song, and which is not an easy song to play, especially when you get into the channo. You better know your right changes. But Jimmie Noone, he was such a great guy and I wrote some things with him. I don't -- whatever he asked me to write because I used to play with him in Chicago.
You had permission to write these things, yes.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: emulate this man's sound. This man had one of the greatest sounds on the clarinet, and even when you hear Benny Goodman play 'Sweet Lorraine' today you'll hear Jimmy Noone.

ctx.x: With Woody Herman I wrote a tune for Auld Woody Herman when I was arranger for Georgia Auld All. And Woody Herman at this time was recording the different tenor players with his band, and he had recorded Georgia Auld All and I wrote Auld a tune for Georgia Auld All called Concerto for Tenor, a tenor saxophone. That Georgia recorded with him and then I recorded with Woody Herman and wrote an arrangement on Don Redman's Cherry, and recorded that. Ben Webster also recorded with him at this time, and with Gene Krupa…

So with Ina Rae Hutton, I forget what I used to write for her, but I used to -- Dizzy Gillespie was writing for WHEN Boyd Ina Rae, I was writing for Ina Rae, she would come in. Board Rabin, Dizzy Gillespie, Tad Damon and myself, we were --and I don't want to forget this guy's name, I'll recall it in a Boyd Rabin minute. We were all writing for Board Rabin. Jimmy Noone --
So just bring it on down from there.

Well, I wrote for Gus Arnner and and I wrote for him (inaudible). I wrote for Earl Hines; I wrote for Jerry Jerome as I told you as staff arranger for NBC. I wrote for Billy Eckstein, Sarah Vaughn, and I wrote for Teddy Wilson when he was at CBS with his program. And I wrote for Fletcher Henderson, I wrote for Dizzy Gillespie, I wrote for Woody Herman, I wrote for Gene Krupa, I wrote for Auld George Yorks, I wrote for Ina Rae Hutton, I wrote for Boyd Rabin, and I wrote for Jimmy Noon.
